templates.name: HR, hiring
templates.aim: Fill critical roles and get every new hire through their first month.
templates.verifiedBy: Applicant tracking system, signed contracts, payroll start date
templates.stallRule: A candidate with no new step in 7 days

ladder.asks: Which roles got new applicants, from where?

ladder.needs: Screen call held, notes on fit
ladder.asks: Who did you screen, and what's your read?
Who interviewed them, and what did each say?
What did the references confirm or worry you about?
What did you offer, and when do they decide?
Did they sign? When do they start?
Did they start on the agreed day?
What's left on their 30-day plan?

howClaimsGetInflated.name: Pipeline padding
howClaimsGetInflated.says: Candidates counted before anyone has screened them.

howClaimsGetInflated.name: Waiting on the hiring manager
howClaimsGetInflated.says: Stuck without a date asked for.

howClaimsGetInflated.name: Started = onboarded
howClaimsGetInflated.says: Day one counted as the finish line.

rulesALeadMightSay.said: “A hire isn't done until they've finished their first month.”
rulesALeadMightSay.means: Onboarded needs the 30-day plan signed off

rulesALeadMightSay.said: “No offer without two references.”

templates.name: Finance, collections and close
templates.aim: Collect on time, close the month by day 5, explain every transaction.
templates.unitOfWork: Invoice, per debtor; the month-end close checklist
templates.rollsUpBy: Debtor and age of the debt
templates.verifiedBy: Accounting system, bank statements, M-Pesa records
templates.stallRule: A promised payment date passes without payment

ladder.asks: Which invoices went out today?
Which debts fell due?
Who got a reminder?
Who did you speak to, and what did they say?
What date did they promise?
What came in, against which invoice?

howClaimsGetInflated.name: Chased by email only
howClaimsGetInflated.says: A reminder counted as a conversation.

howClaimsGetInflated.name: Promised, no date
howClaimsGetInflated.says: “They'll pay soon” with nothing to hold them to.

howClaimsGetInflated.name: Close done, reconciliation not
howClaimsGetInflated.says: Books closed with items still unexplained.

rulesALeadMightSay.said: “If they miss a promised date, it goes to me.”
“We close by the fifth, whatever happens.”

templates.name: Procurement
templates.verifiedBy: Purchase orders, delivery notes, supplier invoices

ladder.asks: What was requested today?
How many quotes, and from whom?
Why this supplier?
Which orders went out?
Did they confirm the date in writing?
What arrived, and was it complete?
Was anything wrong with it?

howClaimsGetInflated.name: Single quote
howClaimsGetInflated.says: One quote treated as a comparison.

howClaimsGetInflated.name: Verbal dates
howClaimsGetInflated.says: A delivery date nobody wrote down.

howClaimsGetInflated.name: The supplier is always late
howClaimsGetInflated.says: Recurring failure blamed, never acted on.

rulesALeadMightSay.said: “Nothing over KES 100K without three quotes.”
“Late twice and we find a backup.”
rulesALeadMightSay.means: A supplier late twice in 8 weeks needs a backup

templates.name: Marketing
templates.aim: Generate demand that sales actually accepts.
templates.shape: Ladder across the handoff to sales
templates.stallRule: A live campaign with no accepted leads in 2 weeks

ladder.asks: What's the hypothesis?
What went live?
How many leads, from where?
How many met the criteria?
How many did sales accept, and why were others rejected?
Which became real deals?

howClaimsGetInflated.name: Vanity leads
howClaimsGetInflated.says: Counted, never accepted by sales.

howClaimsGetInflated.name: Stopped with no reason
howClaimsGetInflated.says: A campaign ended with nothing learned.

howClaimsGetInflated.name: Attribution by hope
howClaimsGetInflated.says: Every deal credited to the last campaign.

rulesALeadMightSay.said: “A lead only counts if sales takes it.”
“Every campaign gets a hypothesis.”

templates.name: Customer success
templates.aim: Keep customers, and notice risk before renewal.
templates.stallRule: No contact in 30 days with an at-risk account

ladder.asks: Where is each new account in onboarding?
Which accounts dropped in usage?
What's the risk, in their words?

ladder.needs: Actions with an owner and date
ladder.asks: Who owns the save, and by when?
Did they renew?
Why did they leave?

howClaimsGetInflated.name: Healthy by assumption
howClaimsGetInflated.says: No contact in 60 days, still marked healthy.

howClaimsGetInflated.name: Save plan with no owner
howClaimsGetInflated.says: A plan nobody's doing.

howClaimsGetInflated.name: Churn reason: price
howClaimsGetInflated.says: The default reason, never checked.

rulesALeadMightSay.said: “Anyone renewing in 60 days gets a call.”
“No usage for two weeks means at risk.”
rulesALeadMightSay.means: At risk after 2 weeks without usage

templates.name: Legal and compliance
templates.aim: Keep contracts reviewed and close compliance gaps.
templates.stallRule: A review open longer than 5 days

ladder.asks: What came in?
What risks did you find?

ladder.needs: Changes sent to the other side
ladder.asks: What are we asking to change?
What was agreed?
Is it signed?
Is the renewal date in the calendar?

howClaimsGetInflated.name: Reviewed, no flags
howClaimsGetInflated.says: A review with no risks written down.

howClaimsGetInflated.name: Waiting on the other side
howClaimsGetInflated.says: No date asked for.

howClaimsGetInflated.name: Filed, not diarised
howClaimsGetInflated.says: Signed but the renewal date isn't anywhere.

rulesALeadMightSay.said: “Anything with unlimited liability comes to me.”
“Every contract gets a renewal date on day one.”

templates.name: Research and data
templates.aim: Produce analysis people can trust and act on.
templates.verifiedBy: Repository and version history, reviewer sign-off
templates.stallRule: A dataset that hasn't moved in 10 days

ladder.asks: Where is the data from?
What did you collect?
What did you fix?
Who validated it, and what did they check?
What did you find?
Who got it?
What did they decide with it?

howClaimsGetInflated.name: Self-validated
howClaimsGetInflated.says: Checked by the person who cleaned it.

howClaimsGetInflated.name: Findings without sources
howClaimsGetInflated.says: A number with no trail back.

howClaimsGetInflated.name: Published = used
howClaimsGetInflated.says: Delivery counted as impact.

rulesALeadMightSay.said: “Nobody validates their own data.”
“Every chart says where the number came from.”

templates.name: Enterprise sales
templates.aim: Close large deals where the buyer is a committee, not a person.
templates.verifiedBy: CRM, calendar, signed contracts, procurement portal
templates.stallRule: The decision date moves twice, or 14 days with no contact

ladder.needs: Org chart, who buys, who uses
ladder.asks: Who's in the buying group?

ladder.needs: The problem in their words, and its cost
ladder.asks: What does this problem cost them?

ladder.needs: A named insider who acts for you
ladder.asks: What did your champion do for you this week?
Who was in the room?
Have you met the person who signs?
What's the decision date, and has it moved?
Which procurement step are you at?
What's still open, and what's the competitor offering?
Is it signed?

howClaimsGetInflated.name: Champion by hope
howClaimsGetInflated.says: A friendly contact who can't move the deal.

howClaimsGetInflated.name: The moving date
howClaimsGetInflated.says: A decision date that slips every month.

howClaimsGetInflated.name: Competitor unknown
howClaimsGetInflated.says: “No one else is bidding.”

rulesALeadMightSay.said: “No champion, no forecast.”
rulesALeadMightSay.means: A deal needs a champion to count in the forecast

rulesALeadMightSay.said: “If the date moves twice, it's not this quarter.”
rulesALeadMightSay.means: Decision date moved twice: out of this quarter

templates.name: Project manager
templates.aim: Deliver the project on time and within budget, with every change to the plan agreed.
templates.verifiedBy: Signed deliverables, invoices, the project plan's version history
templates.stallRule: A milestone date passes, or moves without being re-agreed

ladder.asks: Which milestones are due in the next 2 weeks?
Who's working on it, and is the date still real?

ladder.needs: A named reason and a new date asked for
ladder.asks: What's the risk, and what date would you commit to now?
What was handed over, to whom?
Who signed it off?
What did it cost against the budget line?

howClaimsGetInflated.name: % complete
howClaimsGetInflated.says: A number with no deliverable behind it.

howClaimsGetInflated.name: The date that quietly moves
howClaimsGetInflated.says: Slipped without anyone re-agreeing it.

howClaimsGetInflated.name: Delivered, not accepted
howClaimsGetInflated.says: Handed over but never signed off.

rulesALeadMightSay.said: “If a date moves, I want to hear it from you, not the plan.”
“Nothing counts until the client signs it off.”

templates.name: Product manager
templates.aim: Launch something customers use, with every decision traceable to evidence.
templates.verifiedBy: Product analytics, customer interviews, release notes
templates.stallRule: A decision with no evidence behind it, or a launched feature with no usage check after 2 weeks

ladder.needs: A named customer, the problem in their words
ladder.asks: Which customers told you what?

ladder.needs: How many share it, and how it's measured
ladder.asks: How many customers have this, and how do you know?

ladder.needs: What was decided, why, and what would prove it wrong
ladder.asks: What did you decide, and what would change your mind?

ladder.needs: Shipped behind a flag or to beta
ladder.asks: What shipped?

ladder.needs: Used by the people it was for
ladder.asks: Who is using it after 2 weeks?
Did they keep using it?

howClaimsGetInflated.name: Loudest customer
howClaimsGetInflated.says: One request treated as demand.

howClaimsGetInflated.name: Shipped = done
howClaimsGetInflated.says: Launch counted as success, usage never checked.

howClaimsGetInflated.name: Decision without a test
howClaimsGetInflated.says: Nothing named that would prove it wrong.

rulesALeadMightSay.said: “We don't build for one customer.”
“Every feature gets a usage check at two weeks.”

templates.name: New market launch
templates.aim: Launch in a new country with every workstream ready on the same date.
templates.verifiedBy: Licences, signed partner agreements, hires' contracts, CRM
templates.stallRule: A dependency another team owns with no date for 3 days

ladder.asks: Which workstreams are behind their plan?

ladder.needs: Another team named, with a date
ladder.asks: Who are you waiting on, and did they give a date?
What moved this week?
What still stops it being ready?
Is it signed off for launch?

howClaimsGetInflated.name: Blocked on “them”
howClaimsGetInflated.says: A dependency with no named team or date.

howClaimsGetInflated.name: Ready by feel
howClaimsGetInflated.says: Called ready with no checklist.

howClaimsGetInflated.name: Each team on track, launch late
howClaimsGetInflated.says: Every workstream green, but not on the same date.

rulesALeadMightSay.said: “Every dependency has a name and a date, or it's a risk.”
rulesALeadMightSay.means: Dependencies need an owner and date

rulesALeadMightSay.said: “Ready means the checklist, not the owner's word.”

templates.name: Field officer, registrations
templates.aim: Register traders and keep them active, market by market.
templates.verifiedBy: Registration records, profile photos, first transaction in the app
templates.stallRule: A registered trader with no activity after 14 days

ladder.needs: Market, date, how many traders spoken to
ladder.asks: Which markets, and how many traders did you speak to?
How many registered, and which market?
How many profiles are complete?
Who hasn't used it yet, and why?
Who stopped, and what did they say?

howClaimsGetInflated.name: Registrations without activity
howClaimsGetInflated.says: Numbers up, nobody using it.

howClaimsGetInflated.name: Market-day spikes
howClaimsGetInflated.says: One big day hiding four empty ones.

howClaimsGetInflated.name: Same market every week
howClaimsGetInflated.says: Easy markets revisited, hard ones skipped.

rulesALeadMightSay.said: “A trader only counts when they've used it once.”
“Every market gets a second visit within a month.”

templates.name: Government approval, stakeholders
templates.aim: Build the relationships and confirm the real approval pathway, stakeholder by stakeholder.
templates.shape: Stakeholder grid, showing who made each step happen
templates.unitOfWork: Stakeholder; the approval pathway, held as an assumption until confirmed
templates.rollsUpBy: Role in the decision (decides or influences) and office
templates.verifiedBy: Calendar invites, letters and replies, meeting notes, official documents such as terms of reference
templates.stallRule: A stakeholder with no step in 3 weeks, or a commitment carried 3 check-ins

ladder.needs: Named, with their role in the decision
ladder.asks: Who else decides this, and who told you?
Who did you write to, and did they reply?
Who set the meeting up: you or us?

ladder.needs: They replied or came back themselves
ladder.asks: Did they get back to you on their own?

ladder.needs: Understood the proposal before the formal meeting
ladder.asks: What did they understand before the workshop?
What have they done for us since?

howClaimsGetInflated.name: Letters as relationships
howClaimsGetInflated.says: A letter counted as engagement.

howClaimsGetInflated.name: One-source pathway
howClaimsGetInflated.says: A process mapped from one conversation.

howClaimsGetInflated.name: Borrowed meetings
howClaimsGetInflated.says: Meetings the organisation set up, reported as his.

rulesALeadMightSay.said: “If the pathway only comes from one person, it isn't confirmed.”
rulesALeadMightSay.means: The pathway needs two sources, one official

rulesALeadMightSay.said: “I shouldn't have to chase you.”
rulesALeadMightSay.means: The organisation's chasers are recorded as dependency
